Exploratory data analysis: UCI Heart Disease, four hospitals¶

Input: data/processed/heart_clean.csv, produced by the validation gate (make prepare); its SHA-256 is recorded in data/processed/validation_report.json. Run: make eda executes this notebook and writes every figure to reports/figures/.

Scope (decision D1): the model is trained on Cleveland only; Hungary, Switzerland and VA Long Beach are held back for external validation. Sections 1–3 and 7 therefore compare sites, while sections 4–6 look at the Cleveland training population.

Educational project: not a medical device and not medical advice.

In [1]:
import json
import textwrap
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from IPython.display import Image, display

from heartrisk import viz
from heartrisk.config import load_config
from heartrisk.data.clean import load_clean, read_site
from heartrisk.data.schema import CODE_LABELS, DESCRIPTIONS, FEATURES

ROOT = Path.cwd().resolve()
ROOT = ROOT.parent if ROOT.name == "notebooks" else ROOT
CONFIG = load_config(ROOT / "configs" / "data.yaml")
FIGURES = ROOT / "reports" / "figures"
SITES = list(CONFIG["sites"])
SITE_LABELS = {site: spec["label"] for site, spec in CONFIG["sites"].items()}
viz.apply_style()
pd.set_option("display.precision", 1)



def publish(fig, name, alt):
    # Save the figure for the report, then show that exact PNG here, with alt text.
    path = viz.save_fig(fig, name, FIGURES)
    plt.close(fig)
    display(Image(filename=str(path), alt=alt, width=760))


def wrap(text, width=28):
    return "\n".join(textwrap.wrap(text, width))


df = load_clean(ROOT / "data" / "processed" / "heart_clean.csv")
gate = json.loads((ROOT / "data" / "processed" / "validation_report.json").read_text())
cleveland = df[df["site"] == "cleveland"]
print(
    f"{len(df)} rows from {df['site'].nunique()} sites | gate: {gate['status']} | "
    f"heart_clean.csv sha256 {gate['output']['sha256'][:16]}..."
)

920 rows from 4 sites | gate: pass | heart_clean.csv sha256 0d99bda801da97be...

1. Dataset overview per site¶

One row per hospital. "Missing" counts both ? in the source files and zeros that the site used to mean "not measured" (decision D2).

In [2]:
by_site = df.groupby("site", sort=False)
gaps = df[FEATURES].isna()
overview = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "Rows": by_site.size(),
        "Disease %": by_site["target"].mean().astype(float) * 100,
        "Rows with a missing value %": gaps.any(axis=1).groupby(df["site"], sort=False).mean() * 100,
        "Features > 50% missing": (gaps.groupby(df["site"], sort=False).mean() > 0.5).sum(axis=1),
        "Severity 0-4 recorded": by_site["num_raw"].max().gt(1).map({True: "yes", False: "0/1 only"}),
    }
).rename(index=SITE_LABELS)
overview

2. Missingness: as recorded, and after decoding each site's conventions¶

The left panel counts only the explicit ? markers. The right panel also treats a zero cholesterol or resting blood pressure as missing, because no living patient has either value. Switzerland looks complete on cholesterol until its zeros are decoded.

In [3]:
recorded = pd.concat(
    {
        SITE_LABELS[s]: read_site(ROOT / "data" / "raw" / f"{s}.data", CONFIG["missing_token"])[FEATURES].isna().mean() * 100
        for s in SITES
    },
    axis=1,
)
decoded = gaps.groupby(df["site"], sort=False).mean().T.rename(columns=SITE_LABELS) * 100

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(7.5, 5.8), sharey=True)
for ax, (title, table) in zip(axes, [("As recorded ('?' only)", recorded), ("After decoding zeros (D2)", decoded)]):
    image = ax.imshow(table.to_numpy(), cmap=viz.SEQUENTIAL, vmin=0, vmax=100, aspect="auto")
    ax.set_xticks(range(table.shape[1]), table.columns, rotation=35, ha="right")
    ax.set_yticks(range(len(FEATURES)), FEATURES)
    ax.grid(False)
    ax.set_title(title)
    for i, j in np.ndindex(table.shape):
        value = table.iat[i, j]
        if value >= 1:  # label only non-trivial cells; blank means complete
            ax.text(j, i, f"{value:.0f}", ha="center", va="center", fontsize=11,
                    color="white" if value >= 55 else viz.INK)
fig.colorbar(image, ax=axes, label="% of rows missing", shrink=0.75)
fig.suptitle("Missing values per feature and site")
publish(fig, "eda_01_missingness",
        "Two heatmaps of percent missing per feature and site. Cleveland is almost complete; "
        "ca and thal are mostly missing at the other three sites; Swiss cholesterol goes from "
        "0% to 100% missing once its zeros are decoded.")

3. Class balance¶

Left: the share of patients with disease differs by site far more than sampling noise would explain. Right: in Cleveland the diagnosis num has five levels; the binary target used throughout this project is target = 1 for any num > 0, so each bar is coloured by the class it maps to.

In [4]:
fig, (ax_site, ax_sev) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(7.5, 3.6), width_ratios=[1.3, 1])

share = by_site["target"].value_counts(normalize=True).unstack()[[0, 1]] * 100
counts = by_site.size()
ypos = np.arange(len(share))[::-1]
left = np.zeros(len(share))
for cls in (0, 1):
    ax_site.barh(ypos, share[cls], left=left, height=0.62, color=viz.CLASS_COLORS[cls],
                 label=viz.CLASS_LABELS[cls], edgecolor=viz.SURFACE, linewidth=2)
    left += share[cls].to_numpy()
for y, site in zip(ypos, share.index):
    ax_site.text(share.loc[site, 0] + share.loc[site, 1] / 2, y, f"{share.loc[site, 1]:.0f}%",
                 ha="center", va="center", color="white", fontsize=11, fontweight="bold")
ax_site.set_yticks(ypos, [f"{SITE_LABELS[s]} (n={counts[s]})" for s in share.index])
ax_site.set_xlim(0, 100)
ax_site.set_xlabel("% of patients")
ax_site.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
ax_site.set_title("Disease prevalence by site")

severity = cleveland["num_raw"].value_counts().sort_index()
ax_sev.bar(severity.index.astype(int), severity.to_numpy(), width=0.68,
           color=[viz.CLASS_COLORS[int(k > 0)] for k in severity.index])
for k, v in severity.items():
    ax_sev.text(int(k), v + 3, str(v), ha="center", fontsize=11, color=viz.INK_SECONDARY)
ax_sev.set_xticks(range(5))
ax_sev.set_ylim(0, severity.max() * 1.12)
ax_sev.set_xlabel("Diagnosis code num")
ax_sev.set_ylabel("Patients")
ax_sev.grid(axis="x", visible=False)
ax_sev.set_title("Cleveland severity")

fig.legend(*ax_site.get_legend_handles_labels(), loc="outside upper center", ncol=2)
publish(fig, "eda_02_class_balance",
        "Left: stacked bars of disease prevalence per site, from 36% in Hungary to 93% in "
        "Switzerland. Right: Cleveland diagnosis codes 0 to 4; code 0 maps to no disease and "
        "codes 1 to 4 to disease.")

4. Continuous measurements in Cleveland, by class¶

Outline histograms (normalised to density, so the two classes are comparable despite different sizes). The panel text gives each class median.

In [5]:
continuous = ["age", "trestbps", "chol", "thalach", "oldpeak"]
fig, axes = plt.subplots(3, 2, figsize=(7.5, 8.4))
for ax, col in zip(axes.flat, continuous):
    data = cleveland[[col, "target"]].dropna().astype(float)
    edges = np.histogram_bin_edges(data[col], bins=16)
    for cls in (0, 1):
        ax.hist(data.loc[data["target"] == cls, col], bins=edges, density=True, histtype="step",
                linewidth=2, color=viz.CLASS_COLORS[cls], label=viz.CLASS_LABELS[cls])
    medians = data.groupby("target")[col].median()
    ax.set_ylim(0, ax.get_ylim()[1] * 1.25)  # headroom so the median text never sits on a bar
    ax.text(0.98, 0.97, f"median {medians[0]:g} vs {medians[1]:g}", transform=ax.transAxes,
            ha="right", va="top", fontsize=11, color=viz.INK_SECONDARY)
    ax.set_title(DESCRIPTIONS[col])
    ax.set_yticks([])
    ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
legend_ax = axes.flat[-1]
legend_ax.axis("off")
legend_ax.legend(*axes.flat[0].get_legend_handles_labels(), loc="center", title="Cleveland, n = 303")
fig.suptitle("Distribution by class (medians: no disease vs disease)")
publish(fig, "eda_03_continuous_cleveland",
        "Five outline histograms for Cleveland comparing patients with and without disease. "
        "Patients with disease are older, reach a lower maximum heart rate and show more ST "
        "depression; blood pressure and cholesterol overlap heavily.")

5. Categorical features in Cleveland: disease rate per category¶

Each bar is the share of patients in that category who have disease; the grey line is the overall Cleveland rate. Category sizes are in the labels, because a striking rate on a handful of patients is weak evidence.

In [6]:
categorical = ["sex", "cp", "fbs", "restecg", "exang", "slope", "ca", "thal"]
panel_titles = {  # hand-broken where the long category labels leave little title width
    "fbs": "Fasting blood sugar\n> 120 mg/dl",
    "slope": "Peak-exercise\nST-segment slope",
    "ca": "Vessels coloured\nby fluoroscopy",
}
overall = 100 * cleveland["target"].mean()
fig, axes = plt.subplots(4, 2, figsize=(7.5, 10))
for ax, col in zip(axes.flat, categorical):
    stats = cleveland.groupby(col)["target"].agg(["mean", "size"])
    ypos = np.arange(len(stats))[::-1]
    rates = 100 * stats["mean"].astype(float)
    ax.barh(ypos, rates, height=0.62, color=viz.CLASS_COLORS[1])
    ax.axvline(overall, color=viz.INK_MUTED, linewidth=1.2)
    for y, rate in zip(ypos, rates):
        ax.text(rate + 2, y, f"{rate:.0f}%", va="center", fontsize=11, color=viz.INK_SECONDARY,
                zorder=3, bbox={"facecolor": viz.SURFACE, "edgecolor": "none", "pad": 1})
    ax.set_yticks(ypos, [f"{CODE_LABELS[col][int(k)]} (n={n})" for k, n in stats["size"].items()])
    ax.set_xlim(0, 118)
    ax.set_xticks([0, 50, 100])
    ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
    ax.set_title(panel_titles.get(col, DESCRIPTIONS[col]))
fig.suptitle(f"Disease rate per category (line: overall {overall:.1f}%)")
publish(fig, "eda_04_categorical_cleveland",
        "Eight bar panels of Cleveland disease rate per category. Rates well above the overall "
        "45.9% appear for asymptomatic chest pain, exercise-induced angina, one or more coloured "
        "vessels and a reversible thallium defect.")

6. Rank correlation in Cleveland¶

Spearman's $\rho$ over the continuous, binary and ordinal columns plus the target. The nominal codes (cp, restecg, slope, thal) are left out: their numbers are labels, not quantities, so a rank correlation on them would be meaningless; section 5 covers them instead.

$$\rho = 1 - \frac{6 \sum_{i=1}^{n} d_i^2}{n\,(n^2 - 1)}$$

Notation: $\rho$ = Spearman rank correlation (unitless, from −1 to +1); $d_i$ = difference between the ranks of patient $i$ on the two variables; $n$ = number of patients with both values present. (With tied ranks, pandas computes $\rho$ as the Pearson correlation of the ranks, which the formula above equals when there are no ties.)

In [7]:
columns = ["age", "sex", "trestbps", "chol", "fbs", "thalach", "exang", "oldpeak", "ca", "target"]
rho = cleveland[columns].astype(float).corr(method="spearman")
shown = rho.iloc[1:, :-1]  # drop the empty first row and last column of the lower triangle
mask = np.triu(np.ones(shown.shape, dtype=bool), k=1)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 6.4))
image = ax.imshow(np.ma.masked_array(shown.to_numpy(), mask), cmap=viz.DIVERGING, vmin=-1, vmax=1)
for i, j in np.ndindex(shown.shape):
    if not mask[i, j]:
        value = shown.iat[i, j]
        ax.text(j, i, f"{value:+.2f}".replace("-", "−"), ha="center", va="center", fontsize=11,
                color="white" if abs(value) >= 0.5 else viz.INK)
ax.set_xticks(range(shown.shape[1]), shown.columns, rotation=35, ha="right")
ax.set_yticks(range(shown.shape[0]), shown.index)
ax.grid(False)
ax.spines[["left", "bottom"]].set_visible(False)
fig.colorbar(image, ax=ax, label="Spearman ρ", shrink=0.8)
ax.set_title("Cleveland: rank correlation (lower triangle)")
publish(fig, "eda_05_correlation_cleveland",
        "Lower-triangle heatmap of Spearman correlations in Cleveland. The target correlates "
        "most with ca, exang, oldpeak and, negatively, with maximum heart rate; cholesterol and "
        "fasting blood sugar are close to zero.")

rho["target"].drop("target").sort_values(key=abs, ascending=False).map("{:+.2f}".format).rename("ρ with target").to_frame()

7. Site shift: are the external sites the same population?¶

If the hold-out hospitals differed from Cleveland only by chance, external validation would be a formality. They do not.

In [8]:
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(7.5, 6.4), sharey=True)
ypos = np.arange(len(SITES))[::-1]  # Cleveland at the top, as in section 3
row = dict(zip(SITES, ypos))
for ax, col in zip(axes.flat[:3], ["age", "thalach", "chol"]):
    groups = {s: df.loc[df["site"] == s, col].dropna().astype(float) for s in SITES}
    present = [s for s in SITES if len(groups[s])]
    ax.boxplot([groups[s] for s in present], positions=[row[s] for s in present], widths=0.5,
               orientation="horizontal", patch_artist=True,
               boxprops={"facecolor": "#e7e9eb", "edgecolor": viz.NEUTRAL, "linewidth": 1.2},
               medianprops={"color": viz.INK, "linewidth": 2},
               whiskerprops={"color": viz.NEUTRAL, "linewidth": 1.2},
               capprops={"color": viz.NEUTRAL, "linewidth": 1.2},
               flierprops={"marker": "o", "markersize": 4, "markerfacecolor": viz.NEUTRAL,
                           "markeredgecolor": "none", "alpha": 0.6})
    low, high = ax.get_xlim()
    ax.set_xlim(low, high + 0.3 * (high - low))  # room on the right for the counts
    for s in SITES:
        text = f"n={len(groups[s])}" if len(groups[s]) else "not recorded"
        x = high + 0.28 * (high - low) if len(groups[s]) else (low + high) / 2
        ax.text(x, row[s], text, ha="right" if len(groups[s]) else "center", va="center",
                fontsize=11, color=viz.INK_MUTED)
    ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
    ax.set_title(wrap(DESCRIPTIONS[col]))

ax = axes.flat[3]
asymptomatic = df.groupby("site", sort=False)["cp"].apply(lambda s: 100 * (s == 4).mean()).reindex(SITES)
ax.barh([row[s] for s in SITES], asymptomatic.to_numpy(), height=0.55, color=viz.NEUTRAL)
for s, value in asymptomatic.items():
    ax.text(value + 2, row[s], f"{value:.0f}%", va="center", fontsize=11, color=viz.INK_SECONDARY)
ax.set_xlim(0, 100)
ax.set_xlabel("% of patients")
ax.grid(axis="y", visible=False)
ax.set_title("Asymptomatic chest pain\n(cp = 4)")
axes.flat[0].set_yticks(ypos, [SITE_LABELS[s] for s in SITES])
fig.suptitle("Site shift across the four hospitals")
publish(fig, "eda_06_site_shift",
        "Horizontal box plots of age, maximum heart rate and cholesterol per site, and the share "
        "of asymptomatic chest pain per site. VA patients are oldest; Switzerland and VA reach "
        "lower heart rates; Swiss cholesterol was not recorded; asymptomatic chest pain rises "
        "from 42% in Hungary to 80% in Switzerland.")

8. Findings that feed the modelling choices¶

The numbers below are computed here, so the findings that follow can be checked against them.

Findings¶

# Finding (numbers from the tables above) Consequence for modelling
1 Cleveland is almost complete: 2.0% of rows have a missing value (ca 1.3%, thal 0.7%). At the other three sites 99.5–100% of rows have one, and three features are more than 50% missing at each Imputation lives inside the model pipeline, fitted on training folds only; the external sites will be scored mostly on imputed ca and thal
2 ca is the strongest single signal in Cleveland (ρ = +0.49) and is missing for 96–99% of external patients Expect a real drop in external performance; test missing-value indicators (D3) and a model that handles missing values natively (HistGradientBoosting, D4)
3 Prevalence ranges from 36.1% (Hungary) to 93.5% (Switzerland), against 45.9% in Cleveland Precision and accuracy move with prevalence, so external results are compared on ROC-AUC, which does not (D5), and each site's prevalence is reported next to its metrics
4 Other strong Cleveland signals: exercise-induced angina (ρ = +0.43; 77% disease vs 31%), maximum heart rate (ρ = −0.42), ST depression (ρ = +0.41), asymptomatic chest pain (73% vs 45.9% overall), reversible thallium defect (76%). Cholesterol (+0.12), resting blood pressure (+0.13) and fasting blood sugar (+0.03) are weak The clinically expected predictors dominate. Switzerland's missing cholesterol costs little
5 The external sites are different populations: median age 49 (Hungary) to 60 (VA) vs 56; median maximum heart rate 120–121 at Switzerland and VA vs 153; asymptomatic chest pain 79.7% (Switzerland) and 65.5% (VA) vs 47.5% Covariate shift is built in; Switzerland and VA traffic drives the drift demonstration in the monitoring stage
6 Cleveland's classes are close to balanced: 164 without disease, 139 with (num 1–4 pooled) No resampling; stratified cross-validation keeps the 54/46 ratio in every fold
7 Some categories are tiny: resting ECG "ST-T abnormality" has n = 4, thallium "fixed defect" n = 18 One-hot encoding must tolerate unseen categories (handle_unknown="ignore"); rates on such small groups are not evidence
8 Continuous features span very different scales (ST depression 0–6.2 mm, cholesterol 126–564 mg/dl) Standardise inside the pipeline for logistic regression; tree models are unaffected by scaling
